Lean Lukasiewicz: K, Peirce, composition and S in 56 steps instead of 107

Lukasiewicz.lean derived K, S, Peirce and composition from modus ponens and the unrestricted
Lukasiewicz row by porting the 107-certificate condensed-detachment DAG of Jeff's CD254.v.
Its namespace is now rendered from a 56-step derivation (rho8cd/derivation_luk.txt) found by
rho8cd's search (cdr with UNR=1 NOZ=1 and the four goals), seeded with the 107 CD254
statements as hints:

  four goals, CD254 hints               97 nodes
  hint deletion                         97 -> 83 -> ... -> 71 (stalled)
  three goals (no composition)          97 -> 59
  four goals, union of both as hints    58, then hint deletion -> 57 (56 lemmas + the row)

  Lukasiewicz.lean  524 lines / 28,731 bytes -> 314 lines / 15,764 bytes

The public statements (Implicational, k, peirce, composition, s) are unchanged and the Tarski
bridge after the namespace is byte-identical. Checked: lake build of Lukasiewicz and of every
module importing it (Code254, KCode222, KThmK, Numeric254, TarskiFalsity); every formula of the
derivation is a classical tautology.

rho8cd: generate_domrho8_cd.py gains --luk (rewrites the namespace in place, keeping the tail)
and --rocq-cd (the same derivation as the Rocq CD222.v); the --rocq, --core and --luk outputs
reproduce the committed files byte for byte. cdr gains UNR=1 (row without side condition);
search/hints_cd254.txt holds the seed hints.

Rocq, as a proposal for the peer's checkpoint (user directive: Rocq production stays with the
peer): rho8cd/rocq-proposal/ holds CD222.v (22,865 -> 12,007 bytes; compiled with Prop222,
G222, Interp222 and Complete222, all closed under the global context) and DomRho8.v (22,673 ->
11,190 bytes; compiled with ThmDom).

K215 Lean: cut the old 254-state program proof out of the endpoint's import closure

Adopted from batch 212's semantic-proof packet (proposals/semantic-proof/proposals/import_cut): ConstructibleChoice imported ZFNative only for ZFNative.models_ZF, which pulled in the whole 254-state program calibration, and KQ1ZF reached the same layer through an unneeded WFTheory import. models_ZF moves verbatim into the new ZFModelSemantics (same namespace and name; ZFNative imports it, so legacy clients are unchanged), ConstructibleChoice imports ZFModelSemantics and KQ1ZF imports WFModel.

KEndpoint215's import closure drops from 180 to 169 modules: Dag254, DecodeFresh254, L2Axioms254, L2AxiomsEval254, L2Control254, L2Lib254, L2Macros254, L2Root254, NativeDecoded254, NativeTheory254, WFTheory and ZFNative leave; ZFModelSemantics enters. Checked: lake build of ZFModelSemantics, ZFNative, ConstructibleChoice, KQ1ZF and KEndpoint (112 jobs); no module of the remaining closure outside KEndpoint's imports an edited module except KEndpoint215, and none names a declaration of the removed modules. The full KEndpoint215 rebuild (its stale K215 chain) is not run here.

K215 Lean: one 58-step derivation for both implicational calculi

Following batch 212's shared-core proposal (proposals/shared-proof-core, shared-implication):
the dominated core and the unrestricted Lukasiewicz basis now come from one condensed-detachment
derivation. rho8cd's search (NOZ=1, goals: the row, composition, prefixing, K, Peirce, S; seeded
with both previous derivations and the packets' 63-step one) gives 68 nodes, and hint deletion
59 nodes: 58 lemmas, the same count as the three-goal core, so K, Peirce and S cost nothing
(the packets reach 63 by appending five steps).

DominatedImplication.lean renders it (--core), exporting k, peirce and s beside rho8_all,
composition and lift_right; all six depend on no axioms. The Lukasiewicz namespace becomes an
adapter: a Language whose domination relation holds everywhere, so every row is restricted and
the core's theorems are the unrestricted K, Peirce, S and composition. Its public statements and
the Tarski bridge after the namespace are unchanged.

  DominatedImplication.lean   330 lines / 14,739 bytes (phase ten) -> 308 / 14,410
  Lukasiewicz.lean            314 lines / 15,764 bytes             -> 101 /  4,097
  both                        644 lines / 30,503 bytes             -> 409 / 18,507

Checked: lake build of DominatedImplication, DomRho8, KCodeDom, Lukasiewicz, Code254, KCode222,
KThmK, Numeric254, TarskiFalsity and KEndpoint; every formula of the derivation is a classical
tautology. The producer still reproduces the earlier 58-step three-goal core of d93adc4174 byte
for byte, and gains the k/peirce/s exports when a derivation has those goals.

Phase eleven inlined two single-use final aliases by hand. The renderer now does this generally: when a goal's lemma is no other lemma's premise, the public theorem applies modus ponens to that lemma's premises at the goal's own instance. On the shared core this inlines rho8_all and s: DominatedImplication.lean 308 -> 300 lines (14,410 -> 14,146 bytes), 58 -> 56 private lemmas. Only --core output changes; the Rocq renderings in rocq-proposal/ reproduce byte for byte. K215 Lean: drop the 254 enumerator from the endpoint's import closure

Enum254 (the abstract six-register enumerator of the 254-state machines, 718 lines) reached KEndpoint215 through two imports that do not need it: L2Lib222 imported it but uses only Code254 (which Enum254 itself imports), and QuotientZF0 imported it for two corollaries that nothing calls. generate_l2k222.py now rewrites the forked import to Code254 (it reproduced all three forks byte for byte before the change, and the change is that one line); enum_halts_of_zf0_refutation and zf0_consistent_of_enum_nonhalting move verbatim, same namespace and names, into the new QuotientZF0Enum254, which the ZFC facade imports.

KEndpoint215's closure: 169 -> 168 modules. Checked with the serial driver, one lean process at a time: L2Lib222, L2Macros222, QuotientZF0, ProgramZF0, WFModel and QuotientZF0Enum254 compile. ZFCBoundPerm252 (outside the K215 closure, no caller of the moved theorems) was not rebuilt: its stale 252-lane chain was stopped. A static scan of the remaining closure (imports whose module's declarations are never named) found no further cut: its four candidates are used transitively or through open.
